decision: every transcendental call of the engine goes through pse-fmath (pure-Rust libm by default; feature platform-libm reproduces the host C library byte for byte), so results depend on the locked crates and the Rust toolchain only; tests/fixtures/pure_libm.json is the platform-independent golden fixture (its 16 seeded graph histories are identical to the Windows fixture, as they involve no transcendental function); the Windows fixture is retained unchanged and compared only on request (ignored test)
explanation: the state digest covers the data helix (circular mean of phases through sin, cos and atan2), the carrier phase ladder (sin, cos), the gate metrics q, k, g (exp, cos) and, through the adaptive calibrator's rolling history and the archive, everything derived from them; C libraries round these functions differently in the last bit, and the digest is maximally sensitive to that bit (one ulp in sin changes 73 of 78 digests and 6 crystal digests), so platform arithmetic is a sufficient explanation of the historical mismatch; the fixture does not record component values, so the specific Windows library results cannot be reproduced here
